cleanIntro: The A-Bolt is a three-lug, 60-degree-lift bolt rifle with a thumb-operated top-tang "safety" and a detachable box magazine that clips to a hinged floorplate. Its published strip is one operation, the bolt out of the receiver, and that is what opens the chamber and bore for cleaning. Two things set it apart from the later X-Bolt: on the A-Bolt the safety locks the bolt closed when it is on safe, and the bolt comes out with the safety OFF safe while you press the FRONT end of the bolt stop. The one part the book does have you take apart is the magazine: bottom plate, spring and follower.

steps.title: Muzzle safe, finger off the trigger, and read the safety by its letter
steps.action: Point the rifle in a safe direction and keep your fingers out of the trigger guard. The safety is the thumb slide on the top tang behind the receiver. Drawn rearward it is on safe: an "S" shows on the tang, the trigger is blocked and the bolt is locked closed. Pushed forward the "S" is covered and a red dot shows, and the rifle is ready to fire.
steps.prose: On an A-Bolt a bolt handle that will not lift is the safety doing its job, not a stuck action. Do not read the rifle's condition off the red dot or the red cocking indicator alone; Browning warns that time, weather and cleaning agents wear the red off.
steps.quote: When the “safety” is drawn to the rear, the firearm is in the on safe position (Figure 2). This blocks the trigger and locks the bolt in the closed position.
steps.cite: Browning A-Bolt Rifle Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — OPERATION OF THE "SAFETY"
steps.warn: WARNING: DO NOT DEPEND ON THE RED COLOR ALONE TO INDICATE YOUR FIREARM’S SAFETY STATUS.

steps.title: Bolt open, chamber emptied, and look in
steps.action: Open the bolt and draw it fully rearward so any cartridge in the chamber is ejected, and leave it back with the action open. Then look into the chamber and see that it is empty. Browning's own unloading order is chamber first, then the magazine, so the round most likely to fire is the first one dealt with.
steps.prose: Because on safe locks the bolt closed, the handle will only lift once the safety is forward; keep the muzzle safe and your finger out of the guard while it is, and return the safety to on safe as soon as the chamber is empty.
steps.quote: Open the bolt and eject any cartridge in the chamber. Leave the bolt in the rearward position with the action open.
steps.cite: Browning A-Bolt Rifle Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — UNLOADING > UNLOADING THE RIFLE, step 1
steps.warn: An ejected round you did not see land is still somewhere. Find it before you go on.

steps.title: Floorplate down, magazine off the floorplate
steps.action: Press the magazine latch at the front of the trigger guard and let the hinged floorplate swing down with the magazine on it. Grasp the sides of the magazine toward the front and pull it off the floorplate. With the chamber empty and the magazine off, the bolt can be closed.
steps.prose: The A-Bolt magazine is not a drop-out box: it clips to the floorplate by a small lip at its rear and snaps on at the front. Taking the magazine off proves nothing about the chamber, which is why that came first.
steps.quote: Press the magazine latch in front of the trigger guard and allow the hinged floorplate-magazine unit to swing downward.
steps.cite: Browning A-Bolt Rifle Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — UNLOADING > UNLOADING THE RIFLE, step 3
steps.warn: Remember, merely removing the magazine does not mean the chamber is unloaded.

steps.title: Strip the magazine and every spare
steps.action: Push forward on the rim of the top cartridge and slide it out of the magazine, then the next, one at a time, until the magazine is empty. Unload any extra magazines at the same time. Count what comes out against what you loaded: four in a standard caliber, three in magnums, Micro Medallion, 284 Win., WSM and WSSM, plus one in the chamber.
steps.prose: Then put every cartridge away from the bench. Browning's cleaning warnings say to keep all ammunition away from the cleaning area.
steps.quote: Strip the cartridges from the magazine by pushing forward on the rim of the top cartridge and slide each cartridge out of the magazine, one at a time.
steps.cite: Browning A-Bolt Rifle Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — UNLOADING > UNLOADING THE MAGAZINE, step 2

steps.title: Bolt out: safety off safe, handle up, press the FRONT of the bolt stop
steps.action: Look into the chamber once more and confirm it is empty. Put the safety in the off safe position, because on safe locks the bolt, and rotate the bolt handle up. The bolt stop is the horizontal bar on the left side of the receiver: press inward on its front end and carefully draw the bolt rearward and out. Put the safety back on safe once the bolt is clear.
steps.prose: As the bolt clears, lift it away rather than letting it drop back: the serrated cocking indicator under the bolt shroud is what hits the comb. On a left-hand rifle the bolt is on the left side of the receiver; Browning illustrates the right-hand rifle.
steps.quote: The bolt stop is the horizontal bar on the left side of the receiver (Figure 6). Press inward on the front end of the bolt stop and carefully draw the bolt to the rear and out of the receiver.
steps.cite: Browning A-Bolt Rifle Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — INSERTING AND REMOVING THE BOLT > REMOVING THE BOLT, step 3
steps.warn: WHEN REMOVING THE BOLT FROM THE RECEIVER, TAKE CARE TO PREVENT THE COCKING INDICATOR FROM STRIKING AND DAMAGING THE COMB OF THE STOCK.

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: You have the rifle with its action open and floorplate down, the bolt whole, and the magazine. That is the whole of the A-Bolt's published strip: barrel, receiver and stock stay together and the bolt is not taken apart. Clean after every day of shooting, and more often if the rifle gets excessively dirty.
steps.prose: A minimum session is a wipe-down and oil on the key parts; regular maintenance adds the bore. Deep Clean covers the one further take-apart Browning publishes, the magazine.
steps.quote: Clean your firearm after every day of shooting, and more often if it becomes excessively dirty. A minimum cleaning includes wiping down the firearm and oiling key parts. Regular maintenance will also include cleaning the barrel.
steps.cite: Browning A-Bolt Rifle Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — CLEANING AND MAINTENANCE SUGGESTIONS > CLEANING PROCEDURES

deepSteps.title: When the magazine needs it: inspect often, clean at 500 to 1000 rounds
deepSteps.action: Look at the magazine often. Lubricant and dirt gather in it gradually, and Browning's normal interval for taking it apart to clean is after 500 to 1000 cartridges fired. Work with the magazine off the floorplate and every cartridge out of it.
deepSteps.prose: A follower that hangs or a top round sitting crooked is the sign it is due early.
deepSteps.quote: Frequently inspect magazines to determine the need for cleaning as lubricant and dirt will gradually collect in the mechanism. Normally, the magazine should be cleaned after firing 500 to 1000 cartridges.
deepSteps.cite: Browning A-Bolt Rifle Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — CLEANING THE MAGAZINE

deepSteps.title: Bottom plate out to the rear
deepSteps.action: Hold the empty magazine and slide its bottom plate out toward the rear. Keep a thumb over it as it comes free, because the magazine spring is under it.
deepSteps.prose: Browning wants eye protection on for cleaning and disassembly in case springs or spring-tensioned parts get loose.
deepSteps.quote: Slide the magazine bottom plate out to the rear.
deepSteps.cite: Browning A-Bolt Rifle Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — CLEANING THE MAGAZINE, step 2
deepSteps.warn: WEAR EYE PROTECTION WHEN DISASSEMBLING AND CLEANING YOUR RIFLE TO PREVENT THE POSSIBILITY OF SPRINGS, SPRING-TENSIONED PARTS, SOLVENTS OR OTHER AGENTS FROM CONTACTING YOUR EYES, RESULTING IN INJURY.

deepSteps.title: Spring and follower out for inspection
deepSteps.action: With the bottom plate off, lift out the magazine spring and the follower. Look the spring over for kinks or a collapsed coil, and the follower for burrs or wear.
deepSteps.prose: Note which way round the follower and spring sat before they came out; they go back the same way.
deepSteps.quote: The magazine spring and follower can then be easily removed for inspection.
deepSteps.cite: Browning A-Bolt Rifle Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — CLEANING THE MAGAZINE, step 3

deepSteps.title: Wipe, a very thin coat of oil, wipe again
deepSteps.action: Wipe the dirt and residue off the body, spring and follower. Apply a very thin coat of oil, then wipe it off again. The magazine should be left almost dry.
deepSteps.prose: Extra oil in a magazine only holds fouling and dirt, which is what you just took out.
deepSteps.quote: Wipe off any dirt or residue, then apply a very thin coat of oil and wipe clean again. Too much oil will only serve to collect fouling and dirt.
deepSteps.cite: Browning A-Bolt Rifle Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — CLEANING THE MAGAZINE, step 4

deepSteps.title: Spring and follower back in, bottom plate slid home
deepSteps.action: Put the spring and follower back into the magazine and slide the bottom plate back into position from the rear until it is fully seated. Press the follower down once to feel the spring push it back up.
deepSteps.prose: Browning's text reads "slide the. bottom plate"; the stray full stop is theirs.
deepSteps.quote: To reassemble, reinsert the spring and follower, then slide the. bottom plate back into position (Figure 18).
deepSteps.cite: Browning A-Bolt Rifle Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — CLEANING THE MAGAZINE, step 5

deepSteps.title: No further disassembly
deepSteps.action: The magazine is the last thing Browning has you take apart. The bolt is not stripped, and nothing in the trigger or action is disassembled for cleaning. If further disassembly for service or cleaning is needed, the rifle goes to a qualified gunsmith or to Browning's service facility in Arnold, Missouri.
deepSteps.prose: Browning also forbids altering the trigger, the safety or any part of the firing mechanism, under any circumstances.
deepSteps.quote: NEVER ATTEMPT TO TAKE YOUR FIREARM APART FURTHER THAN EXPLAINED IN THIS OWNER’S MANUAL. YOUR FIREARM IS A SPECIALIZED, FINELY FITTED MECHANISM. YOU MAY PERMANENTLY DAMAGE IT BY ATTEMPTING TO DISASSEMBLE THE INNER MECHANISM ASSEMBLIES.
deepSteps.cite: Browning A-Bolt Rifle Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — CLEANING THE MAGAZINE, closing notice

cleaning.name: BORE AND CHAMBER
tasks: ⛔ Safety on safe, action open, rifle confirmed unloaded before any cleaning
Rod with a tip and patch large enough for a snug fit, entered at the breech end
Run the patch back and forth several times; a patch saturated with nitro solvent lifts normal powder residue
Never let the rod strike the muzzle crown; damage there can affect accuracy
Heavy fouling: bronze bore brush dipped or sprayed with nitro solvent, pushed completely through before it is drawn back
Copper solvent through the bore to its maker's procedure; magnum calibers need it more often
Wipe the chamber and bore dry, then one slightly oiled patch through for preservation
Check the barrel and chamber for a patch left behind

cleaning.name: RECEIVER AND BOLT
tasks: Small brush or rag to lift dirt and foreign matter out of the receiver and the rest of the action
A very light film of light gun oil on the moving parts, used sparingly
Do not pour oil into the receiver; it drains into the wood, softens it and loosens the stock
The bolt is cleaned whole; Browning publishes no bolt disassembly

cleaning.name: MAGAZINE
tasks: Inspect often; normally cleaned after 500 to 1000 cartridges
Each cartridge base flush with the rear of the magazine when reloading, nose not past the front

cleaning.name: METAL AND STOCK
tasks: Wipe exposed metal with a lightly oiled cloth and remove every finger mark
Wood: light gun oil or furniture wax, not both
Oil-finish wood that is spotted or dull: rubbing alcohol on a lint-free cloth, dry, then a linseed-oil-based finish
Camouflage, Dura-Touch and other special finishes: no solvents or strong chemicals; light solvent-free oil or a damp cloth with mild dish soap, water kept out of the action

cleaning.name: LEAVE ALONE
tasks: ⛔ No disassembly beyond the bolt out and the magazine apart
⛔ Never alter the trigger, the safety or any part of the firing mechanism
Do not snap the firing pin on an empty chamber

reassembly: Magazine: spring and follower back in, bottom plate slid back into position.
Confirm the chamber and bore are empty and that no patch is left in the barrel.

Bolt cocked before it goes in: the cocking indicator shows at the rear of the bolt. If it does not, turn the rear section of the bolt clockwise (seen from the indicator end) until the firing pin sear engages the notch in the bolt handle.
Safety in the off safe position.
Lugs on the bolt sleeve aligned with the lugs on the bolt.
Forward end of the bolt into the rear opening of the receiver; pressing the bolt stop is not needed but eases it. Push the bolt fully forward and rotate the handle down to lock it.
Immediately put the safety in the on safe position.
Magazine back on the floorplate: the small lip on its rear face into the groove at the back of the floorplate, then snap the front firmly into place.
Swing the floorplate and magazine up until the magazine catch retains them.
⛔ Never test the mechanical function of the rifle with live ammunition.
fncheck: With no ammunition anywhere near the bench, look through the bore and confirm it is clear and that no patch is left in the barrel or chamber. With the safety off safe, cycle the bolt a few times and confirm it runs and locks down cleanly, then put the safety on safe and confirm the "S" shows and the bolt handle will not lift. With the rifle cocked, confirm the serrated cocking indicator can be seen and felt below the bolt shroud. Swing the floorplate up and confirm the magazine catch holds it. If a scope is mounted, check inside the receiver that no base screw is long enough to reach the bolt. Do not dry-fire it to check the trigger: Browning's rule is never to snap the firing pin on an empty chamber. If something will not work after a thorough clean, the rifle goes to a Browning Recommended Service Center, Browning's Arnold, Missouri facility, or a qualified gunsmith.
